claims.statement: The `step ca` group is registered in command/ca/ca.go with 16 subcommands: health, init, bootstrap, token, certificate, rekey, renew, revoke, provisioner, sign, root, roots, federation, acme, policy, and admin.
The `step ca` group defines shared flag variables used across subcommands: ACME options (--acme, --contact, --http-listen, --standalone, --webroot), --fingerprint, --kid, and the SSH --host flag.
step ca health makes an API request to the /health endpoint of the Step CA to check whether it is running.

step ca init initializes the CA PKI for an offline authority, with flags for root/key generation, PKI and SSH options, Helm output and deployment type, dns/address endpoints, initial provisioner, RA and KMS selection, remote management, ACME, and profile/authority selection.

step ca bootstrap downloads the root certificate to <$STEPPATH/certs/root_ca.crt> and writes <$STEPPATH/configs/defaults.json> with the CA URL, root location, and fingerprint, so later commands need not pass --ca-url, --root, or --fingerprint; --install installs the root into the system's default trust store.
step ca root downloads and validates the root certificate, step ca roots downloads all root certificates, and step ca federation downloads all federated certificates.

step ca token generates a one-time token granting access to the CA, with flags for --san, --principal, --not-before, --not-after, --key, --output-file, and action qualifiers --revoke, --renew, --rekey, and --ssh.

step ca certificate creates a certificate through the selected provisioner flow, supporting --san plus device-attestation flags --attestation-ca-url, --attestation-ca-root, hidden --attestation-ca-insecure, and --tpm-storage-directory (default <$STEPPATH>/tpm), and the shared ACME flags.
step ca sign generates a new certificate from signing a certificate request.
step ca rekey rekeys a certificate, with flags --out-cert, --out-key, --private-key, --expires-in, and reload hooks --pid, --pid-file, --signal, --exec, --daemon, --rekey-period.
step ca revoke revokes a certificate by serial number or via --cert/--key files, recording an optional --reason or --reasonCode.

step ca renew renews a certificate and writes the new chain over the original file or to --out; by default it authenticates with mTLS, while --mtls=false or an already-expired certificate falls back to an X5C token flow using a JWT with issuer step-ca-client/1.0 and an x5c header carrying the certificate chain.

In daemon mode, step ca renew schedules renewals via nextRenewDuration: without flags the deadline is one third of the validity period before expiration (renewal at the 2/3 point), a random jitter of up to period/20 is applied, --expires-in overrides the deadline, and --renew-period overrides the period.

renewer.Daemon blocks on a timer plus SIGINT/SIGTERM (exit) and SIGHUP (immediate renewal), logging each successful renewal to stdout and errors to stderr, and force overwrite is always enabled in daemon mode.
After each renewal, getAfterRenewFunc runs the reload hooks: it sends a signal (default SIGHUP) to the PID from --pid or --pid-file and then executes the --exec command if set.

newRenewer builds the renewal client: with --offline (and required --ca-config) it uses cautils.NewOfflineCA wrapping the local authority; otherwise it creates an online ca.NewClient with a transport pinned to the root file, attaching the client certificate only while still valid.
step ca provisioner manages provisioners with the subcommands list, jwe-key (retrieve and print a provisioner's encrypted provisioning key), add, update, remove, and webhook.

step ca provisioner add supports the default JWK type plus typed provisioners acme, sshpop, x5c, k8ssa, oidc, aws, azure, gcp, scep, and nebula; ACME provisioners accept challenges http-01, dns-01, tls-alpn-01, and device-attest-01, and SCEP provisioners accept attestation formats apple, step, and tpm.

step ca provisioner webhook manages webhooks attached to a provisioner (add/update/remove); webhook response data is exposed to certificate templates under Webhooks.<name>, with endpoint flags --url, --kind, --bearer-token-file, --basic-auth-username, --basic-auth-password-file, --disable-tls-client-auth, and --cert-type.
step ca policy manages certificate issuance policies at three levels: authority, provisioner (requires --provisioner), and acme (requires --provisioner plus --eab-key-reference or --eab-key-id).

The active policy level is carried in the Go context via policycontext (authorityPolicyLevel, provisionerPolicyLevel, acmePolicyLevel), and the shared action code retrieves the linkedca.Policy for the level, creating a new empty policy when the CA reports it does not exist yet.

X.509 policies expose allow (with cn, dns, email, ip, uri), deny, and wildcards subcommands; SSH policies expose host and user scopes; each name action accepts --remove to delete values instead of adding them, view prints the current policy, and remove deletes the whole policy.
The provisioner- and ACME-level policy command groups document that certificate issuance policies at those levels are currently only supported in Certificate Manager.

step ca admin manages admins with list, add, remove, and update; admins are addressed by <subject> <provisioner>, can be created with --super, and operations run through a linkedca *ca.AdminClient created with cautils.NewAdminClient, combining linkedca.Admin fields with the provisioner name and type.
BetaCommand() exposes only the ACME command under step beta ca, which is registered by command/beta/beta.go; there is no command/beta/ca directory.
